papers.title_en: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
papers.authors: Xuanang Gao, Zhiwei Ning, Gengming Zhang, Jiaxi Cao, Runze Yang, Zhonglong Zheng, Jie Yang, Rong Xiao, Wei Liu
papers.evidence: 利用SAM物体先验的自监督单目深度估计
papers.tldr: 现有自监督深度估计普遍缺少物体级信息，导致恶劣条件下物体内部深度易偏移、边缘易模糊，鲁棒性不足。RoSAMDepth借助SAM的物体级先验，设计分段引导表征对比、自适应区域离群掩码结合区域高斯似然损失，并进行物体级可靠性估计。多数据集和多种天气实验表明，该方法输出更锐利、更准确的深度，稳定超越现有方法，为鲁棒自监督深度估计提供了有效框架。
papers.abstract_en: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/xagao/RoSAMDepth.

papers.title_en: Efficacy of Monocular Depth Estimation in Lunar Environments
papers.authors: Michael W. Lanighan, Kenji Brameld, Seth Gee
papers.evidence: 单目深度估计泛化性评估
papers.tldr: 单目深度估计在陆地同分布场景已取得高精度，但其在月球等分布外环境是否有效仍待验证。本文利用NASA Ames POLAR立体数据集与Apollo 17月面影像，建立从模拟到实地的验证流程，结合物理真值定量评估和历史影像定性比较。结果表明，部分先进方法可泛化到非结构化月面，生成高保真相对三维重建。该工作为月球探测中的单目深度估计提供了跨域验证范式。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in monocular depth estimation have demonstrated highly accurate 3D reconstructions within in-distribution terrestrial domains. This study investigates the efficacy of several state-of-the-art approaches to reconstruct out-of-distribution lunar environments using the NASA Ames Polar Optical Lunar Analog Reconstruction (POLAR) stereo dataset and Apollo 17 surface imagery. By leveraging these datasets, we establish a robust analog-to-field validation pipeline that evaluates quantitative performance against ground-truth physical analogs and qualitative performance against historical field data. Our results indicate that select state-of-the-art techniques can successfully generalize to produce high-fidelity relative 3D reconstructions of the unstructured lunar surface.

papers.title_en: CASE: Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars
papers.authors: Yi-Jen Tsai, Yen-Yu Lin, Chien-Yao Wang
papers.evidence: 使用正负视觉示例的概念感知少样本语义分割
papers.tldr: 现有少样本语义分割多依赖单一类别的正样本，难以处理“红车”与所有车、车辆与应排除对象等歧义。作者提出正负视觉提示共同定义目标的SVPS设定，并构建基于COCO和PACO的CASE基准，覆盖排除、隔离、并集及属性级六类任务。评测发现冻结SAM 3不能稳定将负提示作为排除证据，进而提出保守LoRA适配的CPA基线。该方法提升正负提示解释能力，同时在仅正样本少样本分割中保持竞争力。
papers.abstract_en: Few-shot semantic segmentation typically identifies target objects based on positive support examples of a single semantic class. In practice, however, positive cues alone are often underspecified: for instance, "red cars" may be confused with cars of all colors, "vehicles" may include cars that should be excluded, and "material-defined objects" may span multiple categories. Fulfilling precise requests requires positive exemplars to provide inclusion evidence and negative exemplars to act as intent-defining constraints for exclusion and disambiguation. We formulate this setting as Specified Visual Prompt Segmentation (SVPS), where the target concept is specified by both positive and negative visual prompts. In this work, visual exemplars refer to support-image regions specified by bounding-box prompts. To study SVPS, we introduce CASE (Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars), a benchmark built on COCO and PACO. CASE encompasses six category- and attribute-level task families: exclusion, isolation, union, attribute exclusion, attribute isolation, and attribute union. We evaluate SAM 3 under this setting and find that, despite its powerful positive-only few-shot segmentation capability, frozen SAM 3 does not consistently treat negative visual prompts as exclusion evidence. To address this, we present Concept Prompt Adaptation (CPA), a conservative LoRA-based adaptation baseline that improves positive-negative prompt interpretation on CASE while remaining competitive under positive-only few-shot segmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/WongKinYiu/FSS-CASE.

papers.title_en: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors: Yansong Bai, Yunzhi Zhuge, Xinzhuo Yu, Lu Zhang, Jin Zhan, Pingping Zhang, Huchuan Lu
papers.evidence: 面向域泛化的语义分割稠密预测
papers.tldr: 域泛化语义分割需在无目标域数据时对未见域做密集预测，现有方法难以兼顾抑制域敏感干扰与保留细粒度空间线索。SIFR 提出频率感知双流框架，以频谱建模统一调控 CLIP 与 DINOv2 的异质先验融合及解码器细化。通过频谱引导不变融合过滤域敏感响应，并用低频统计归一化与自适应频率选择稳定多尺度解码特征。在合成到真实、真实到真实和恶劣天气等基准上取得一致提升，兼顾鲁棒性与分割精度。
papers.abstract_en: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. In this work, we propose SIFR, a frequency-aware dual-stream framework that tackles domain shift at both the fusion and decoding stages. SIFR uses spectral modeling as a unified principle to regulate both heterogeneous prior interaction and dense decoder refinement. Instead of directly fusing frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features, SIFR performs spectral-guided invariant fusion to filter out domain-sensitive responses while preserving complementary semantic and structural information. In addition, SIFR incorporates a spectral decoder refinement module that stabilizes multi-scale decoder features through low-frequency statistics-based normalization and adaptive frequency selection, thereby reducing the propagation of residual domain bias in dense prediction. This design enables SIFR to jointly improve domain robustness and segmentation precision under severe distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple DGSS benchmarks, including synthetic-to-real, real-to-real, and adverse-weather settings, demonstrate consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods.
